name: Brazil Oberon, Cerrado
vendor_notes: Chocolate, nutty, fruity aftertaste; light acidity, sweet, full body. Clean and balanced. Body 7/7, sweetness 6/7, brightness 4/7. Grown 900-1,250 m.
goal: Medium roast: chocolate, nuts and heavy body
rationale: Low-grown (900-1,250 m) natural Brazil: soft, low-density beans that take heat fast, crack a little lower and scorch or tip easily, with plenty of chaff. So it charges cooler (182 C) on a gentler burner, with air raised after dry end for chaff and smoke. The cup is about chocolate, nuts and body, so it goes to a medium roast: DTR ~23% and ~14 C after first crack, with a slow, steadily falling RoR through development to build sweetness without roastiness. FC 186 C is an estimate.
steps: Preheat to 182 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 182. Burner 68%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 108 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 176 C (~6:15): burner 44%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:20 at ~186 C: burner 40%, air 60. Then 36%.
Drop ~9:30 at ~200 C (14 C after FC).

history.note: Initial medium-roast plan for a friend, from the Coffee Bean Corral page and calibration from the 2026-09-29 roasts (TP ~0:40, Honduras FC 188.9 C).

Re-fitted the first 3-4 minutes to five real roasts (2026-09-29 to 10-02): on this roaster TP comes at ~0:35 at 108-116 C (not ~0:42 at ~100 C), RoR is highest right after TP and only falls, dry end lands ~3:35-3:55 and FC ~7:12-7:25 at 187-189 C. Earlier versions put the start 10-20 C too low, which invited cutting heat early and a hot finish. FC temperature, roast level and development are unchanged.
